Hi Alex — thanks for the clear notes and the ramp file. Quick summary below plus a proposed phasing file attached.

Short answers first:
- Redemptions for GCP private offers consume against your Marketplace commitment on the invoice month in which the usage occurs; there can be a short reconciliation window but consumption is reflected in monthly billing (i.e., if you redeem in September it appears on the September invoice).
- To avoid mid-quarter depletion we recommend a front-loaded buffer in the first billing month and weekly utilization checks during the initial ramp.

Proposed phasing (see tessa_gcp_phasing_proposal.xlsx):
1) Month 1 (soft launch): allocate 20% of monthly commit to allow for discovery spikes.
2) Months 2-3 (ramp): move to 35% and 60% respectively, with a safety buffer of 8-10% kept unreconciled to avoid surprises.
3) Months 4-6: increase cadence towards the committed target, with monthly automated alerts when remaining credit < 18% of scheduled plan.

Operational items:
- We'll set up a weekly 30-min touch for the first two months to review actual burn vs plan (Connors to propose recurring calendar).
- Marissa will add the billing waterfall notes and any co-sell timing caveats.
- I'll prepare an amendment for signature to lock the phasing so procurement can map it to their PO.

If that high-level approach looks good I can push the DocuSign amendment by EOD Thursday for your procurement team.

Best,
Tessa

Hi all — quick operational notes from the finance side to avoid any surprises when the Marketplace redemption hits GCP:

- GCP posts consumption to the invoice month; however, depending on when your workloads spike there can be a one-invoice-month reconciliation (billing waterfall) where credits are applied during the next invoice cycle. That is what caused the unexpected adjustment we saw on the last MerchantLane proof-of-concept run.
- Recommend we structure the PO amendment with three explicit drawdown tranches tied to calendar months rather than flexible daily redemption. That reduces day-to-day variability for MerchantLane accounting.
- Suggest moving ~10% of the planned Q3 utilization into early Q4 as a cushion to handle any reconciliation timing. This avoids a gap in capacity if GCP applies credits a month later than expected.

I've uploaded a short note with the waterfall example to the HubSpot company record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/merchantlane — see "billing waterfall" doc under attachments.

I'll mark the specific lines to be added into the amendment draft.

—Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: billing_waterfall_notes.pdf (PDF)
